title: still present since round 4: vacancy/status mutations return Ok unconditionally — nonexistent ids report success
evidence:
archive_vacancy ends: `  #(DemoStore(..store, vacancies: updated), Ok(vacancy_id))` (identical at 1259 restore_vacancy and 1273 close_vacancy); change_status ends: `  #(DemoStore(..store, vacancies: updated), Ok(slug))` — all four mutate via list.map and return Ok with no find check, while update_vacancy does: `  let next = DemoStore(..store, vacancies: updated)
  #(next, find_vacancy(next, vacancy_id) |> result.map(fn(v) { v.vacancy }))` (1215-1216) and publish_vacancy the same at 1231.
detail: list.map leaves the store unchanged when no id matches yet Ok is returned — the error channel is dead; UI toasts success for ids that don't exist.
recommended_fix: Mirror update/publish: bind `let next = DemoStore(..store, vacancies: updated)` and return find_vacancy/find_application-derived Results instead of unconditional Ok.

title: still present since round 4: send_reminder / remind_applicant / send_bulk_invite mutate nothing and return canned counts
detail: Reminders never persist (awaiting rows' reminded/followed_up never flip) and the canned counts fire even for vacancies with zero awaiting rows, contradicting the seeded pool.
recommended_fix: Thread the mutated store back like other mutations, flip reminded/followed_up on static_awaiting rows, and derive counts per vacancy.

title: still present since round 4: create_vacancy derives ids from an 8-char slug with no uniqueness check — the doc comment claims collisions can't happen
detail: Two creates with names sharing an 8-char prefix ("Test Cottage A"/"Test Cottage B") produce the same id — the second silently shadows the first in every lookup, contradicting the comment.
recommended_fix: After deriving the id, append a counter while find_vacancy(store, id) is Ok (id-2, id-3…) before inserting.

title: still present since round 4 (narrowed — W13 fixed load-more/comparison/awaiting/scoring only): demo dispatch arms unpinned — refcheck trio, single mark-read, report download, edit deep-link get_for_edit boot, mark-opened threading
evidence:
fire_demo_refcheck/substitute thread `          demo_store: Some(next),` (demo_update.gleam:808, 845) — reverting to plain `model` stays green: the only refcheck demo pins are store-level, demo_flow_test.gleam:471-473: `  let #(after_skip, _) =
    demo_store.refcheck_action(
      store,` (no client.update in either refcheck demo test), and every client_test refcheck test builds `  model.Model(
    ..model.initial(),` (6375-6376, demo_mode False). demo_deep_link_boot_state_test (548-566) covers only the detail-route NotAsked→Loading flip from a hand-built demo model. No test drives UserClickedNotification, UserClickedDownloadReport, the VacancyEdit get_for_edit entry boot, or the mark-opened store threading via client.update from a demo model.
detail: Reverting these arms' interception or `demo_store: Some(next)` threading keeps the client suite green — the r3-W2 pin pattern was applied to only four of the arms.
recommended_fix: Add dispatch pins (demo model + client.update) for UserSavedRefcheckEdit, UserChoseRefcheckAction(Skip), UserClickedNotification, UserClickedDownloadReport, and the edit deep-link boot.

title: still present since round 4: mark_opened doc claims idempotent Submitted→UnderReview but applies to any status
detail: Doc/behaviour mismatch: a viewed, shortlisted, approved or rejected application 'opened' again snaps back to under_review and logs a second auto event.
recommended_fix: Guard mark_opened: no-op returning the current status unless status == Submitted, or fix the doc.

title: still present since round 4: for_edit reports updated_at: vac.created_at and update_vacancy never bumps any timestamp
evidence:
for_edit: `    total_applications: list.length(v.applications),
    status: vac.status,
    updated_at: vac.created_at,
  ))` — update_vacancy's record update `Vacancy(
              ..old,` writes property_name..status fields but sets no updated_at anywhere in its body (1174-1217).
detail: Editing a demo vacancy shows updated_at equal to created_at forever; the edit-save surface can never demonstrate a fresh timestamp.
recommended_fix: Bump an updated_at on the mutation (e.g. the demo 'now' 2026-08-19) and have for_edit report it.

title: still present since round 4: status_from_slug silently coerces unknown slugs to Submitted
detail: A typo'd slug from UserChangedApplicationStatus/backward-transition silently 'succeeds' as Submitted — an unknown backward stop regresses the row instead of erroring.
recommended_fix: Return Result(ApplicationStatus, Nil) and route Errors through respond_result like the other mutations.

title: still present since round 4: fetch_leaderboard_page ignores its page parameter
detail: Demo 'Load more' (UserClickedLoadMoreApplications passes leaderboard_page + 1) always re-delivers the full first page — pagination is cosmetic.
recommended_fix: Slice demo_store.leaderboard's entries by page (page size matching the real API) or document the single-page cap at the call site.

title: still present since round 4: store_of's None fallback re-seeds on every call without writing back to the model
detail: A None demo_store (invariant-break path) silently re-seeds on every dispatch instead of surfacing once; each seed is wasted work and masks the corruption.
recommended_fix: Persist the fallback (demo_store: Some(store) on first hit) or telemetry-log it so the invariant break is visible.

title: still present since round 4: demo_not_in_demo_toast's id convention is off by one vs add_toast — toast ids can collide
evidence: demo_update.gleam: `  let toast_id = model.next_toast_id + 1` ... `      next_toast_id: toast_id,` — client.gleam add_toast: `  let id = model.next_toast_id` ... `  #(Model(..model, toasts: capped_toasts, next_toast_id: id + 1), dismiss_eff)`.
detail: The fallback toast consumes next+1 but leaves next_toast_id equal to the toast's id, so the NEXT add_toast reuses it — two live toasts share one id and AppDismissToast dismisses both.
recommended_fix: Use add_toast's convention: `let toast_id = model.next_toast_id` and `next_toast_id: toast_id + 1` (or route through a shared toast helper).

title: still present since round 4 (narrowed — the fixtures half now has callers): zero-caller export demo_store.notifications
detail: Unused pub export shipped in the demo store; readers must check which of the two read paths is real. (r4 also cited demo_fixtures.result_to_seed_error — the current seed_error_from_result IS wired at demo_store.gleam:151-163, so only this half remains.)
recommended_fix: Delete the wrapper (callers read store.notifications via notifications_unread).

title: still present since round 4 (narrowed — the rsvp half now bans verbs file-wide): CI fetch ban exempts the whole demo_api.gleam file while its header claims a single documented exception
evidence: test.yml: `FETCH_VIOLATIONS=$(grep -rln "gleam/fetch" client/src/demo/ --include="*.gleam" | grep -v "demo_api.gleam" || true)` — a file-level -v exemption, while demo_api's header claims "the CI grep lint enforces the no-network rule by banning the API-client modules and fetch imports across demo/ — except this one documented static-asset fetch in `download`." (The rsvp half WAS narrowed: `RSVP_VERBS=$(grep -rnE "rsvp\.(send|get|post|put|patch|delete)" client/src/demo/ ...)` bans the verbs everywhere; demo_api's only rsvp use is `case rsvp.parse_relative_uri(url)` at :413.)
detail: A new gleam/fetch usage anywhere else in demo_api.gleam passes CI, contradicting the documented single-function exception; both headers overstate the guard.
recommended_fix: Scope the exemption to the download function (line range or its own module), or reword both headers to 'exempt: demo_api.gleam'.

title: still present since round 4 (narrowed — the store_of half is now centralized): download_timeout duplicated between client.gleam and demo_update.gleam
detail: The timeout wrapper exists twice with diverging signatures (parameterised vs hardcoded 90s); changes to the real one's delay won't reach the demo copy.
recommended_fix: Export the parameterised download_timeout from one module and call it with 90_000 from the demo path.
